design:
Child of the multi-thermo flowsheet epic (bn op-186o).


A unit that **reacts** material must return a **new canonical inventory**.

```
canonical inventory -> thermo/reaction view -> reaction solve
                    -> updated canonical inventory -> destination thermo view
```

**Do not let reaction products exist only inside a package-specific state.** A
product that exists only as a package's internal representation cannot be
conserved, bridged, or audited.

**Element conservation must remain independent of the thermo package.** This is
the invariant that makes reacting units checkable at all: species change, the
elements do not.

Relevant to hydrotreating (#85), Claus (#91), reforming (#105) and every
polymer reactor.


## Constraints

Mature-crate refactor: preserve public constructors, deprecate rather than remove, regression tests before semantic changes. Do not implement AGR/Claus/the refinery here. `develop` only, no push to `main`.

description:
Maintainer direction (2026-08-31): kopitiam-bibliography should become a dependency of kovan-literature, declared as a WORKSPACE dependency in the root Cargo.toml.

WHY IT IS WANTED: op-b1y5's closing comment records the gap -- this workspace has no BibTeX PARSER; kovan_literature::bibtex::to_bibtex only RENDERS KovanDocument -> BibTeX, one-way. GitHub issue #35's "citekey IS the paper id" amendment makes a parser mandatory (citekey uniqueness enforced at ingestion, citekey rename as a transactional repo-wide refactor, bibliography.bib as the single authoritative identity namespace).

kopitiam-bibliography supplies it: src/bibtex/parse.rs:119 `pub fn parse_database(&str) -> Result<BibDatabase, BibtexError>`, plus BibLaTeX/Hayagriva emit, citation graph, identifier/DOI handling. 10,692 lines. Also has an explicitly network-free design (no kopitiam-web; resolution is a ReferenceResolver trait + search_text() seam).

BLOCKER -- NOT PUBLISHED. Verified 2026-08-31:
  - https://index.crates.io/ko/pi/kopitiam-bibliography -> HTTP 404
  - crates.io search for "kopitiam" lists 27 published crates (kopitiam-pdf 0.3.1, kopitiam-ocr 0.1.0, kopitiam-neovim 0.2.4, kopitiam-semantic 0.2.5, ...); kopitiam-bibliography is NOT among them.
  - It exists only in the read-only source clone (~/Documents/fun_projects/kopitiam/crates/kopitiam-bibliography), workspace version 0.2.5.
Nothing can be wired until it is published to crates.io. Same blocking shape as kopitiam-pdf 0.3.2 gating GitHub issue #35 step 11 (kopitiam#96). Per CLAUDE.md's hard boundary, the deliverable here is an upstream publish request, never a path/git dep on the clone and never a local patched build.

LICENCE CONSEQUENCE -- MAINTAINER DECISION NEEDED. kopitiam-bibliography is AGPL-3.0-only (license.workspace = true -> kopitiam workspace license = "AGPL-3.0-only") and pulls kopitiam-pdf + kopitiam-document + kopitiam-ontology. kovan-literature currently inherits this workspace's GPL-3.0-only. Taking the dependency forces kovan-literature to AGPL-3.0-only, making it the SECOND AGPL crate here (CLAUDE.md's Members table currently states kovan is the only one).

Blast radius verified as nil:
  - kovan-literature is UNPUBLISHED (index.crates.io 404) -- no released version to relicense around.
  - Its only workspace dependent is crates/kovan, which is ALREADY AGPL-3.0-only.
So the relicense costs: a crates/kovan-literature/NOTICE, an explicit license = "AGPL-3.0-only" (dropping license.workspace), and updating CLAUDE.md's Members table + the "one crate in this workspace that differs from the default" wording + the "Dependency policy" section.

WORKSPACE-DEPENDENCY REQUEST vs CURRENT POLICY. Root Cargo.toml today has ZERO kopitiam entries -- deliberate. CLAUDE.md's "Dependency policy -- single source of truth" states kopitiam-pdf is declared only in crates/kovan/Cargo.toml because "keeping the dependency crate-local is what stops another crate picking it up (and the AGPL question that comes with it) by accident." The maintainer has asked for a workspace dependency, which reverses that guard. If done that way, CLAUDE.md's dependency-policy section must be updated in the SAME change so the file does not contradict the tree.

STEPS WHEN UNBLOCKED:
 1. Confirm kopitiam-bibliography is published; note the version.
 2. Confirm the licence decision (relicense kovan-literature to AGPL-3.0-only) with the maintainer.
 3. Confirm workspace-table vs crate-local declaration with the maintainer.
 4. Check the dependency chain is Android/Termux-clean (no C/BLAS/GPU/-sys crate) before adding, per the Android hard rule -- kopitiam-pdf already is, kopitiam-document/-ontology not yet checked.

 6. Update crates/kovan-literature/NOTICE, CLAUDE.md Members table + dependency policy, and docs/kovan*.md as applicable.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-11 PREDICTION LOGGED BEFORE MEASURING (workspace hard rule: state the expected sign and magnitude first).

Change under test: pebble_beds::keff_delta gains DeltaDomain{Cube,Sphere} (develop 0cd9a22c), so explicit-TRISO, ring-RPT and naive all now run in the reflective SPHERE r=3 that the OpenMC deck actually used. Previously only the surface-tracked CSG ring-RPT row was on that boundary, so the explicit row had no matched twin and item 5 of the V&V doc's Interpretation ('cube rows sit low, CSG-sphere sits high, so this is not one systematic data bias') rested on comparing two different geometries.

PREDICTIONS:
1. explicit-TRISO sphere > explicit-TRISO cube. Removing the cube-corner FLiBe removes parasitic Li-6/F-19 absorption, so k must RISE. Magnitude taken from the ring-RPT cube->CSG-sphere shift already measured (1.33094 -> 1.39333 = +6239 pcm): expect explicit sphere ~1.396, i.e. +6000 to +6500 pcm above its own cube value. A FALL would mean the sphere reflection is leaking histories and the new domain is wrong.
2. explicit-TRISO sphere vs OpenMC 1.36510: expect +2500 to +3300 pcm, i.e. essentially the SAME offset the ring-RPT CSG row shows against OpenMC (+2854).
3. THE DECISIVE ONE: if (2) holds, then the +2854 pcm is a DATA/PHYSICS bias common to both pebbles, NOT an artefact of the RPT geometry or of its fitted radius, and item 5's 'they bracket OpenMC in opposite directions' is explained purely by the cube's extra coolant. Delta(RPT - explicit) measured in the sphere should then come out SMALL - within a few hundred pcm - and much closer to OpenMC's -31 pcm than the -351 pcm the cube gave.
4. If instead Delta(RPT - explicit) in the sphere is LARGE while each is ~+2900 vs OpenMC, the RPT radius transfer is the problem and the radius search is the fix.

Falsifiable either way. Recording before the numbers land so the interpretation cannot be fitted to them afterwards.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-11 FIRST RESULT, and it contains a surprise that is NOT about the domain change. Reporting before the run finishes so the prediction comment above cannot be edited around it.

explicit TRISO, reflective SPHERE r=3 = 1.38191 +- 0.00193
explicit TRISO, reflective CUBE  h=3 = 1.31813 +- 0.00210

Against the predictions logged before measuring:
P1 CONFIRMED, tightly. sphere - cube = +6378 pcm; I predicted +6000 to +6500 from the ring-RPT cube->CSG shift. The sphere arm is behaving as the cube-corner-coolant argument says it must.
P2 WRONG. I predicted explicit-sphere would sit +2500 to +3300 pcm above OpenMC's 1.36510, i.e. the same offset the ring-RPT CSG row shows (+2854). Measured: +1681 pcm. The explicit pebble is roughly 1170 pcm CLOSER to OpenMC than the ring-RPT pebble is. So the absolute offset is NOT a single data bias shared by both pebbles, and P3's conclusion does not follow.

SEPARATE AND LARGER ISSUE - THE RECORDED BASELINE NO LONGER REPRODUCES. The explicit-cube case is the same problem, same settings, same seed as the run recorded in this bead and in verification_and_validation/ring_rpt/ring_rpt_vs_openmc.md, which gave 1.33445 +- 0.00215 at commit 23cd2549. It now gives 1.31813 +- 0.00210 at 0cd9a22c: Delta = -1632 pcm, about 5.4 sigma. Every outram-mc number in that V&V doc is therefore stale for current develop.

What moved in between: 33 njoy commits (waves 5/6/7). Corroborating signal in the same logs - U-238 RECONSTRUCTION WALL TIME FELL FROM 91.7 s TO 26.8 s (U-235 33.7 -> 24.2 s). A 3.4x speedup on U-238 reconstruction is consistent with a coarser reconstructed grid or a changed thinning bound (waves 3/5 touched BROADR thnmax and the sigfig discontinuity shading), and a changed U-238 grid can absolutely move a pebble k by 1600 pcm through the resonance integral.

NOT YET ESTABLISHED, and I will not assume it: whether the shift is the njoy data change or my own DeltaDomain refactor. The cube path SHOULD be bit-identical (Cube::sample_point issues the same three prn draws in the same order; advance_reflective_cube is the old function renamed), but this session's whole lesson is that reading code does not find defects. Next step is the cheap decisive one, which is also the diagnostic op-mzvp.2.12 already wants: dump reconstructed U-238 sigma_gamma(E) at 23cd2549 and at 0cd9a22c and diff them. No transport needed. If the cross sections differ, it is the data; if they are identical, it is my refactor and I will bisect it.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-11 CORRECTION to my own comment above, before the remaining numbers land.

I wrote that 'the explicit pebble is roughly 1170 pcm CLOSER to OpenMC than the ring-RPT pebble is' and concluded 'the absolute offset is NOT a single data bias shared by both pebbles, and P3's conclusion does not follow.' That inference is NOT SUPPORTED, because it compares across commits: the explicit-sphere +1681 pcm is measured at 0cd9a22c, while the ring-RPT +2854 pcm is the OLD figure from 23cd2549 — and the very same comment establishes that the baseline moved by -1632 pcm between those two commits. Differencing a new measurement against an old one across a known 1632 pcm shift is exactly the mistake the shift was discovered by avoiding.

What actually stands:
- P1 CONFIRMED: sphere - cube = +6378 pcm on the explicit pebble, inside the predicted +6000 to +6500.
- P2 WRONG, and this one IS valid, because both sides are absolute against OpenMC's own published 1.36510 with no cross-commit term: I predicted explicit-sphere would sit +2500 to +3300 pcm above OpenMC; measured +1681.
- P3 UNDECIDED. It needs the ring-RPT sphere number FROM THE SAME RUN, which is still transporting. Only a within-run RPT-minus-explicit and a within-run pair of offsets against OpenMC can say whether the bias is shared.

Nothing about the data-versus-refactor question changes: that is still to be settled by the u238_recon_fingerprint probe (committed, compiles) run in both checkouts.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-11 RESULT — matched geometry, within-run, and it REVERSES the recorded interpretation.

                      Delta(ring-RPT - explicit)
  reflective SPHERE   +163 +- 281 pcm   0.58 sigma   <- OpenMC's own boundary
  reflective CUBE    -1079 +- 301 pcm   3.59 sigma   <- the old comparison
  OpenMC reference      -31 pcm         0.34 sigma

  explicit  sphere 1.38191 +- 0.00193
  ring-RPT  sphere 1.38354 +- 0.00204
  explicit  cube   1.31813 +- 0.00210
  ring-RPT  cube   1.30734 +- 0.00215

THE RING-RPT METHOD IS EXONERATED. On the reference's own geometry it reproduces explicit TRISO to within noise and agrees with OpenMC's -31 pcm. The -351 pcm (and later -736 pcm) residuals recorded in this bead and in ring_rpt_vs_openmc.md, and the interpretation built on them ('RPT has the right effect; magnitude is code-dependent... not expected to reach OpenMC's -31 pcm because the inner radius was fitted by the deck author against OpenMC'), were ARTEFACTS OF THE CUBE DOMAIN. The deck author's 1.4934 cm transfers to this code fine; nothing about the radius needed explaining.

P3 NOW RESOLVES, and in favour of the prediction logged before measuring. Absolute offsets, both within this one run and both on the sphere:
  explicit vs OpenMC 1.36510 : +1681 pcm
  ring-RPT vs OpenMC 1.36479 : +1875 pcm
  difference of the two      :  +194 pcm  (inside noise)
Both pebbles carry the SAME bias. So the absolute offset is a data/physics effect common to the nuclear data, NOT the RPT geometry and NOT its fitted radius. P4 (radius transfer is the problem) is ruled out.

Scorecard against the pre-registered predictions: P1 confirmed (+6378 pcm sphere-cube, predicted +6000..+6500); P2 wrong on MAGNITUDE (+1681 measured, +2500..+3300 predicted); P3 confirmed in substance; P4 ruled out.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE REMAINING WORK: 'RPT radius search' is no longer a fix for a residual that does not exist. It is still worth running once, as a measurement of how code-dependent the equivalence radius is, but it is not on the critical path. The critical path is the shared ~+1700..1900 pcm data bias (op-mzvp.2.12) and the -1632 pcm baseline drift between 23cd2549 and 0cd9a22c, which may well be the same question.

Still transporting: naive-homogenised (both domains) and the CSG six-factor row.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-11 the account CLOSES QUANTITATIVELY — the cube did not shift both pebbles equally, it shifted them differentially, and that differential IS the phantom method error.

  explicit  sphere - cube : +6378 pcm
  ring-RPT  sphere - cube : +7620 pcm
  differential            : +1242 pcm

  Delta(RPT-explicit) cube  : -1079 pcm
  Delta(RPT-explicit) sphere: + 163 pcm
  difference                : -1242 pcm   <- identical, to the pcm

So the whole of the previously-recorded RPT 'method error' is the cube's corner FLiBe, and none of it is RPT.

WHY the two pebbles respond differently, which is the part that makes this an explanation rather than a coincidence: the ring-RPT pebble's fuel is a shell at 1.4934-1.7531 cm, so its fuel sits further from the centre ON AVERAGE than the explicit pebble's, which is dispersed through the whole r < 1.9 cm zone. Fuel nearer the coolant is more sensitive to how much coolant there is, so the cube's extra FLiBe (3 < r < 3*sqrt(3), about 2.3x the volume of the sphere's) penalises the RPT pebble harder. The sign and the ordering both follow from the geometry without fitting anything.

General lesson for this workspace, worth carrying beyond this bead: a domain mismatch between a model and its reference is not safely absorbed into 'an absolute offset we can subtract'. It cancels only for quantities that respond identically in both configurations, and two configurations that differ in WHERE the fuel sits do not. Here it survived the differencing and was read as physics for a week.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-11 DEFECT FOUND, and it is in the example, not the physics. The reflective-sphere domain exposed it by removing the external moderator that had been masking it.

Final rows from the matched run:
  explicit  sphere 1.38191  cube 1.31813   sphere-cube = +6378 pcm
  ring-RPT  sphere 1.38354  cube 1.30734   sphere-cube = +7620 pcm
  naive     sphere 1.25736  cube 1.34137   sphere-cube = -8401 pcm   <- OPPOSITE SIGN

naive-minus-explicit flips from +2324 pcm (cube) to -12455 pcm (sphere). The sphere sign is wrong on its face: homogenising removes the flux depression inside each lump, so fewer resonance absorptions per U-238 atom, so k must RISE. Wang 2014's published InfHomMedium unit-cell bias is +2820 pcm.

ROOT CAUSE: mi::HOMOG is homogenise_by_volume over the FIVE TRISO LAYERS ONLY, with no matrix graphite. That is exactly right for the ring-RPT shell, because rpt_fuel_outer_radius sizes the shell to the total particle volume (pf * r_zone^3), so the shell holds all the particle material at particle density and inventory is conserved. It is WRONG for the naive case, which fills the ENTIRE r < 1.9 cm zone with it. The particles occupy only pf = 0.30 of that zone, so the naive pebble carried 1/pf = 3.33x the heavy-metal inventory of the explicit pebble AND zero internal moderator (the explicit pebble's fuel zone is 70% graphite matrix by volume).

So the naive case was never a homogenisation of the explicit pebble. It was a different reactor, and 'naive - explicit' measured nothing about double heterogeneity.

WHY THE SIGN FLIPS, which is the tell: an over-fuelled ball with no internal moderator depends entirely on EXTERNAL moderation. The cube's corner FLiBe supplies a lot of it, propping k up to 1.34137; the sphere removes most of it and k collapses to 1.25736. The explicit and ring-RPT pebbles are internally moderated by their graphite, so for them removing the cube corners removes mostly ABSORBER (Li-6, F) and k rises. Opposite responses, same change.

AND THE CUBE AGREEMENT WAS A COINCIDENCE. +2324 pcm sitting close to Wang's +2820 is why this survived: a mis-specified model produced a plausible number in the one geometry it was ever run in.

FIXED (not yet re-run): new mi::NAIVE_HOMOG = homogenise_by_volume([(homog, pf), (graphite, 1-pf)]), which conserves both the inventory and the matrix moderator. homogenise_by_volume is linear in atom density, so mixing the already-mixed TRISO material with graphite is identical to mixing all six constituents at once. Compiles; re-running now.

The explicit and ring-RPT conclusions recorded earlier today are UNAFFECTED - neither uses this material.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-11 PREDICTIONS for the corrected naive case, logged before the re-run finishes.

N1. SIGN MUST FLIP BACK TO POSITIVE. naive - explicit > 0 on the sphere. Homogenising removes the intra-lump flux depression at the U-238 resonances, so capture per U-238 atom falls and k rises. A negative value now would mean the fix is wrong or the defect was not the whole story.

N2. MAGNITUDE +1500 to +4000 pcm. Wang 2014's published InfHomMedium unit-cell bias is +2820 pcm on the detailed HTR-10 core; this is a different system (FHR pebble, 19.9% HALEU, pf 0.30, FLiBe) so exact agreement is not expected, but the double-heterogeneity worth of a TRISO pebble sits in this band. If it lands outside, the homogenisation still is not conserving something.

N3. naive sphere - cube MUST NOW BE POSITIVE, roughly +5000 to +8000 pcm, i.e. the same direction and rough size as explicit (+6378) and ring-RPT (+7620). This is the direct test of the diagnosis: the negative -8401 pcm was caused by the naive pebble having no internal moderator, so restoring the matrix graphite must make it respond to the cube corners the way the other two do. If it stays negative, the moderator argument is wrong and I will have mis-diagnosed the cause even though the inventory error is real.

N4. The explicit and ring-RPT rows must reproduce their values from the previous run to within Monte Carlo noise, since neither uses the changed material and the seed is unchanged. Any movement there would indicate the material-index insertion perturbed something it should not have - the new material is appended at index 8, so index 0..7 are untouched, but that is an assumption worth testing rather than asserting.

N4 is the one I would bet against myself on: adding a material changes the MAJORANT (Majorant::bounding scans all materials), and a higher majorant means more virtual collisions and a different RNG consumption pattern per history. So explicit and ring-RPT may shift by pure stream divergence even though the physics is identical. If they move, that is expected and NOT a defect - but the size of the move then bounds how much of any k difference in this study is stream noise rather than physics, which is worth knowing.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-11 CORRECTED RE-RUN. Scoring the four predictions honestly, including a sign error of my own.

  SPHERE (matched to OpenMC)
    explicit  1.38191 +- 0.00193
    ring-RPT  1.38354 +- 0.00204   Delta(RPT-explicit)   =  +163 pcm (0.6 sigma)
    naive     1.35656 +- 0.00243   Delta(naive-explicit) = -2535 pcm (8.2 sigma)
  CUBE
    naive     1.30625 +- 0.00245   Delta(naive-explicit) = -1188 pcm
  naive sphere - cube = +5031 pcm  (was -8401 pcm before the fix)

N3 CONFIRMED: naive sphere-cube is now POSITIVE, +5031 pcm, inside the predicted +5000..+8000, and now in the same direction as explicit (+6378) and ring-RPT (+7620). The moderator diagnosis was right: restoring the matrix graphite made the naive pebble respond to the cube corners the way the internally-moderated pebbles do.

N4 CONFIRMED, and BIT-IDENTICALLY: explicit and ring-RPT reproduced 1.38191 and 1.38354 exactly. I had flagged this as the one I would bet against myself on, reasoning that adding a material changes Majorant::bounding and so the virtual-collision count and RNG stream. Wrong, and the reason is instructive: NAIVE_HOMOG is a DILUTION of materials already in the array (TRISO material + graphite), so its Sigma_t is bounded by the existing maximum and the majorant does not move. The check was still worth making; the worry was not justified.

N1 AND N2 FAILED, AND THE ERROR IS MINE, NOT THE FIX'S. I predicted naive - explicit > 0. That is backwards. Self-shielding REDUCES absorption, and the lumped (explicit) configuration has MORE self-shielding than the homogeneous one, so the explicit pebble captures LESS in the U-238 resonances and sits HIGHER. Homogenising must therefore come out LOWER. This repo already says so in plain words, in examples/htr10_fuel_zone_kinf.rs: 'Homogenising removes that depression, so the homogenised case must come out LOWER.' The measured -2535 pcm is the CORRECT sign; my prediction was the thing that was wrong.

WORSE, AND THIS IS THE PART WORTH LEARNING FROM: I anchored N2's magnitude band on Wang 2014's +2820 pcm InfHomMedium bias. That same file explicitly warns against exactly this comparison: Wang's numbers are MULTIGROUP CROSS-SECTION PROCESSING biases against a continuous-energy reference and 'run the other way'; ours is a continuous-energy GEOMETRIC effect; 'Do not compare the two numbers directly.' I made the comparison the codebase warns about, in a comment recorded on this bead.

CONSEQUENCE FOR MY EARLIER COMMENT: I wrote that the old cube value '+2324 pcm sitting close to Wang's +2820' was why the defect survived review. That reasoning is void - it rests on the same bad comparison. The old cube value was in fact WRONG-SIGNED (positive when the physics demands negative), and that, not its magnitude, should have been the red flag. The defect finding itself is UNAFFECTED: it stands on the inventory argument alone (naive carried 1/pf = 3.33x the heavy metal and none of the 70%-by-volume matrix graphite), which is independent of any sign convention.

THE RESULT THAT MATTERS FOR RPT: on the matched sphere the double-heterogeneity worth is -2535 pcm, and ring-RPT reduces the residual to +163 pcm. RPT REMOVES 94% OF THE DOUBLE-HETEROGENEITY ERROR, and what remains is inside Monte Carlo noise. That is the quantitative case for the method, measured on the reference's own geometry, and it is a cleaner statement than anything previously recorded here.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
THE GRAPHITE THERMAL LAW IS PRICED AND EXCLUDED (2026-09-12, commit e2ef43cf).

Every exclusion in this hunt so far has been an ACCURACY statement -- 'the graphite law is within 0.05 % of THERMR', 'sigma within 0.04 % of NJOY', 'RI +0.00 %'. An accuracy statement cannot bound a residual: it says how wrong a mechanism is, not how much the mechanism is WORTH, and a mechanism worth 300 pcm cannot carry 4000 pcm however wrong it is.

New mode OUTRAM_RINGRPT_FREE_GAS_GRAPHITE=1 in examples/fhr_ring_rpt_endf.rs moves every bound-graphite carbon onto free-gas carbon and runs the pebble with no bound thermal law at all. Same seed, same statistics, CSG case:

  graphite S(a,b)   k_eff (ring-RPT CSG)   p (2-group)   p vs OpenMC
  on  (the deck)    1.40546 +/- 0.00234    0.5256        +8.54 %
  REMOVED           1.40419 +/- 0.00243    0.5238        +8.18 %
  difference        -127 +/- 337 pcm       -0.0018       -0.36 points

Deleting the whole law -- every defect in it, known and unknown, together -- is worth -127 +/- 337 pcm (0.38 sigma). The residual's entire signature (p too high by 8.5 %, epsilon too low by 5.0 %) survives with NO bound law present.

That closes the thermal-kernel line for this pebble, including both defects found against it this week: op-x77y / gh:#190 (emission-table resize, measured -211 pcm here, 1.40757 -> 1.40546) and op-bo02 / gh:#191 (fixed point +1.24 % hot, ~-200 pcm at the measured 52 pcm/K slope). Both real, both worth fixing, neither this residual.

The reason is geometric and should have been checked before any accuracy work: this pebble is 70 % FLiBe by volume, free-gas in BOTH codes, and the bound graphite sits only in the inner core and the 0.1 cm shell.

WHERE THAT LEAVES IT. With no bound law at all, p is still +8.2 % and epsilon still -5.0 %. So the defect is above 0.625 eV, in free-gas kinematics plus reconstructed cross sections. To move p from 0.5256 to 0.4842 needs xi*Sigma_s about 12.8 % LOWER (or RI_eff 12.8 % higher). Both p high and epsilon low say the same thing: neutrons leave the fast group too readily -- too much slowing-down power between ~1 eV and ~1 MeV.

Next measurement in flight: price anisotropic elastic scattering the same way (OUTRAM_RINGRPT_ISOTROPIC_ELASTIC=1, Nuclide::with_isotropic_elastic). It is the mechanism most likely to be mispriced, because the slowing-down verification that covers it (xi/xi_0 = 1.000, eight nuclides) spans 4 eV to 10 keV, where CM scattering is isotropic anyway. The MeV anisotropy that sets the slowing-down power above the resonances -- and sets epsilon -- is unverified.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
RESOLVED 2026-09-12, commit 45f8d72d. The +4000 pcm residual was op-0iaq / gh:#193 -- a threshold reaction with a non-zero cross section BELOW its threshold.

  explicit TRISO   1.40514 -> 1.36041   vs OpenMC  +4004 -> -469 pcm (2.2 sigma)
  ring-RPT         1.40739 -> 1.36394   vs OpenMC  +4260 ->  -85 pcm (0.4 sigma)
  naive homogenised            1.32759   naive-explicit -3282 pcm (11.4 sigma)
Six factors on the reference in all four: eta -0.00 %, f -0.01 %, p +0.04 %, eps -0.08 %.
The V&V gate passes with the recorded values re-baselined and its drift tolerance
tightened 5x (1500 -> 1000 pcm).

The trail that got there -- PRICING mechanisms (running the case twice with the
mechanism off) rather than checking their accuracy:
  graphite S(a,b) -> free gas          -127 +/- 337 pcm
  MF=4 elastic angle -> isotropic       -81 +/- 317 pcm
  target motion -> at rest (control)  -2242 +/- 323 pcm  (6.9 sigma, proves the harness)

Worth keeping: every earlier exclusion in this hunt was an ACCURACY statement, and none
could have found this, because the defect is not an accuracy error. F-19's inelastic

where it should NOT have existed that mattered -- a region no comparison was looking at,
because both sides agreed there was nothing there.

title: Ring-RPT cross-code comparison + verification_and_validation/ring_rpt/ V&V doc

description:
VERIFIED 2026-08-11 by code inspection.

STATE: crates/outram-mc-libs/src/material/thermal.rs is explicit at lines 24-26: 'Scope. Only the incoherent-*inelastic* channel — the one H-in-H2O needs (light water has no thermal elastic). Coherent / incoherent-elastic bound scattering (graphite, ZrH) is deliberately not wired here yet.'

The struct holds only xs_e/xs_sigma (sigma_inel) and emit_tables. Nuclide::with_thermal_scattering (src/material/nuclide.rs:221) attaches one ThermalScattering, and nuclide.rs:331-339 REPLACES the free-gas elastic channel with sigma_inel below the cutoff. For a scatterer whose thermal elastic is non-zero that substitution is doubly wrong: it drops the dominant channel AND removes the free-gas stand-in for it.

WHY IT MATTERS (HTR-10 critical path): for graphite at 0.0253 eV, measured through the njoy port against ENDF/B-VIII.0 tsl-crystalline-graphite (MAT=30): sigma_coh_el = 4.55 b, sigma_inel = 0.49 b. Wiring only the inelastic channel would give a graphite pebble ~11% of its true thermal scattering cross section — a materially wrong thermal spectrum and k_eff, and worse than the free-gas treatment it replaces.

WORK: extend ThermalScattering to carry an optional elastic channel (coherent: pre-tabulated sigma_coh_el(E) plus the Bragg (mu, weight) table per incident energy; incoherent: sigma(E,T) plus equiprobable cosines). At a thermal collision, choose elastic vs inelastic in proportion to their cross sections; an elastic scatter keeps E and samples mu from the Bragg weights (lab frame, no CM transform). Mirror OpenMC src/thermal.cpp ThermalData::sample, which does exactly this elastic/inelastic split. Depends on op-u5ju for the njoy-side surface.

SIZE: medium. Mostly plumbing + one sampling branch, but it changes the ThermalScattering shape and the nuclide.rs cross-section substitution, and needs a test.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-11 (this session; AI-assisted draft, NOT human-reviewed, NOT committed - coordinator holds the diff).

WHAT LANDED
- crates/outram-mc-libs/src/material/thermal.rs: new pub enum ThermalElastic {None, Coherent(CoherentElasticTable), Incoherent(IncoherentElasticTable)} (enum dispatch, no trait objects/Box/lifetimes). ThermalScattering now owns an elastic channel alongside the inelastic one, with elastic_xs(E), total_xs(E) and elastic() accessors. from_endf_file() reads the ENDF tape ONCE and DETECTS the elastic law from the evaluation (MT=2 LTHR=1/3 -> coherent, LTHR=2/3 -> incoherent, absent -> None); its signature is unchanged so every existing caller is source-compatible. NjoyError::NotPorted from a channel constructor is treated as 'this evaluation has no such section'; every other error, notably TemperatureOutOfRange, is propagated rather than silently dropping graphite's dominant channel.
- ThermalScattering::sample() now splits elastic vs inelastic with probability sigma_el/sigma_thermal, mirroring OpenMC src/thermal.cpp:296-302 ThermalData::sample_dist. The coherent branch mirrors src/secondary_thermal.cpp:34-54 CoherentElasticAE::sample (invert the cumulative structure factor, mu = 1 - 2 E_k/E, E_out = E_in).
- COHERENT IS STORED EXACTLY, NOT RESAMPLED. sigma_coh_el(E) is a 1/E sawtooth with 221 discontinuities for graphite, so a log-grid resample would smear every Bragg edge. CoherentElasticTable holds the Bragg-edge table itself (221 (E,sigma) pairs, ~3.5 kB - cheaper than the resample AND exact). Incoherent elastic IS resampled (it is smooth); grid sized by measurement at 400 points.
- crates/njoy-outram-park-fork/src/thermr/scattering.rs: added CoherentElasticScattering::bragg_edge_table() -> Vec<(NeutronEnergy, CrossSection)>, the uom-typed accessor that makes the exact storage possible. Mirrors the OpenMC CoherentElasticXS::bragg_edges()/factors() pair. This is the ONLY njoy-side change; the data/transport boundary is intact (outram-mc still parses no ENDF).
- crates/outram-mc-libs/src/material/nuclide.rs: xs_at_energy's thermal substitution now swaps in th.total_xs(e) = sigma_inel + sigma_el, not sigma_inel alone. THIS IS THE ACTUAL DEFECT THIS BEAD NAMED.

MEASURED (ENDF/B-VIII.0, release mode, 2026-08-11; full methodology + results in the module header of crates/outram-mc-libs/tests/thermal_graphite_elastic.rs, 7 tests, all green)
- Graphite MAT 30, 296 K, barn per carbon atom at 0.0253 eV: sigma_coh_el 4.5514, sigma_inel 0.4863, elastic fraction 0.9035. Confirms the ~90 % figure this bead was filed on.
- Exactness: worst relative deviation of the stored Bragg table vs the njoy surface = 7.67e-16 over 21199 points spanning 1e-4 to 4 eV. Bragg cutoff 1.822327e-3 eV (graphite (002)); sigma_el exactly 0.0 below it.
- Nuclide-level, C0 + graphite table vs bare C0, MicroXS::elastic at 0.0253 eV: free-gas 4.9398, bound-new 5.0378, bound-OLD (inel only) 0.4863. The pre-fix path gave graphite 9.8 % of its free-gas scattering; the fixed path gives 102.0 %.
- Sampling, 200000 draws at 0.0253 eV seed 1: elastic fraction 0.90340 vs cross-section prediction 0.90346 (0.09 sigma on a 6.6e-4 binomial sigma). Mean Bragg cosine -0.02357 vs the analytic sum p_i mu_i = -0.02497 over the 17 open reflections (1.17 sigma on SEM 1.20e-3).
- HTR-10 temperatures at 0.0253 eV: 293.15 K snaps to 296 K (NJOY tolerance) -> 4.5514/0.4863; 393.15 K interpolated -> 4.3849/0.6779; 523.15 K interpolated -> 4.1672/0.9445; 1073.15 K interpolated -> 3.3592/2.0373. Monotone Debye-Waller suppression; 100 K and 2200 K are hard TemperatureOutOfRange refusals.
- LIGHT-WATER REGRESSION: tsl-HinH2O MAT 1 at 293.6 K reports channel 'none', sigma_el identically 0, total_xs == inelastic_xs bit-identical, sigma_inel(0.0253) = 52.1420 b. The existing thermal pincell case is unaffected.
- ZrH MAT 7 (the OTHER elastic law, NOT on the HTR-10 path): channel 'incoherent elastic', sigma_el 55.0151 b/H vs sigma_inel 2.8804 b/H; log-grid resample error 2.61e-4 at 400 points (1.05e-3 at 200 - the grid was sized by this measurement); sampled mean cosine 0.13817 vs the njoy equiprobable-cosine mean 0.14142 (1.26 sigma), forward-peaked as the law requires.

GATES RUN: cargo test -p outram-mc-libs --lib --tests --release = 254 tests, 0 failed. njoy scripts/test.sh full suite = 393 lib + all integration, 0 failed. cargo check -p njoy-outram-park-fork -p outram-mc-libs --all-targets --target aarch64-linux-android --release = clean (NDK-free proxy; no native Termux run was done). cargo doc introduces no new broken intra-doc links.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: no k_eff has been computed with the elastic channel in place, and nothing is wired into pebble_beds yet - that is op-hc2o step 5, still open. The reference for the exactness and cosine gates is this workspace's own njoy port, so they are internal-consistency gates, not an independent NJOY/OpenMC-ACE oracle. NOT closing - human review owed.

notes.content: VERIFIED END-TO-END 2026-08-14 through the pebble-bed k-eigenvalue path.
